title: Switzerland at the World Cup
description: Neutral on the pitch? Hardly — Switzerland have a habit of causing World Cup upsets. Test your knowledge.

questions.q: Switzerland hosted the 1954 World Cup. That tournament featured a record-breaking match — Switzerland vs Austria. What was the score?
questions.explain: Austria beat Switzerland 7–5 in the quarter-final of the 1954 World Cup — still the highest-scoring match in World Cup history. The match saw 12 goals in 90 minutes of extraordinary football.

questions.q: Switzerland reached the round of 16 at the 2022 World Cup. Which Portuguese player scored a hat-trick as Portugal knocked them out?
questions.explain: Gonçalo Ramos — starting in place of the dropped Ronaldo — scored a hat-trick in a 6–1 rout of Switzerland. It was Portugal's biggest ever World Cup win and announced Ramos as a star of the future.

questions.q: Switzerland beat France in the 2021 European Championship in a penalty shootout, having come back from 3–1 down. What was the final score after extra time?
questions.explain: Switzerland drew 3–3 with France after extra time and then won 5–4 on penalties in one of Euro 2020's greatest upsets. Kylian Mbappé missed the decisive penalty for France.

questions.q: Swiss midfielder Granit Xhaka is of which ethnic background, making him one of many 'hyphenated' Swiss players?
questions.explain: Granit Xhaka was born in Switzerland to Albanian-Kosovar parents. Switzerland's squad famously includes many players of Balkan heritage — Xhaka, Shaqiri, Zuber — reflecting Swiss immigration history.

questions.q: Xherdan Shaqiri scored one of the 2014 World Cup's most spectacular goals — a bicycle kick against Honduras. Which Swiss city is he originally from?
questions.explain: Shaqiri grew up in Basel, the city where FC Basel is based — the club that launched his career before moves to Bayern Munich, Liverpool and elsewhere. He was born in Kosovo to Albanian parents.

questions.q: Switzerland won their first World Cup match in how many years when they beat Cameroon at Qatar 2022?
questions.explain: Switzerland beat Cameroon 1–0 to open their 2022 campaign, their first World Cup win in 8 years after struggling to get out of the group in Russia 2018.

questions.q: How many official languages does Switzerland have — reflecting its multicultural make-up?
questions.explain: Switzerland has four official languages — German, French, Italian and Romansh — reflecting its unique multicultural identity. This diversity is also reflected in its multinational football squad.

questions.q: Switzerland's best World Cup finish was fourth place. In which year?
questions.explain: Switzerland finished fourth at the 1954 World Cup on home soil, losing the third-place play-off to Austria 3–1. It remains their best ever finish.

questions.q: At the 2018 World Cup, Switzerland's group stage win over Serbia was marked by a controversial celebration. What did Shaqiri and Xhaka do that caused a political storm?
options: Pointed at the camera to protest racism
Made a double-headed eagle gesture symbolising Albania
Celebrated in front of the Serbian bench
Refused to shake hands with Serbian players
questions.explain: Shaqiri and Xhaka made the two-handed eagle gesture — a symbol of the Albanian flag — after scoring against Serbia, reflecting the Kosovo conflict. Both were fined but not suspended by FIFA.

questions.q: Switzerland qualified for every World Cup between 2006 and 2022 except one. Which tournament did they miss?
options: They qualified for all of them
questions.explain: Switzerland qualified for the World Cup in 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022 — five consecutive tournaments. Their consistent qualification makes them one of Europe's most reliable World Cup teams.
